newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus head to meet EU panel on Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: Airbus head to meet EU panel on Boeing merger.

text.p: The managing director of Airbus Industrie on Friday will present the aircraft consortium's concerns over a planned merger between Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp. to the European Commission, an Airbus spokesman said Thursday.
Jean Pierson and Financial Controller Ian Massey will "provide evidence to the commission's mergers task force" Friday morning, the spokesman said.
The linkup between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas "has long-term implications which are detrimental to competition," he said.

Airbus strongly opposes the merger plan, which will create a $48 billion colossus in defence and civilian markets, dwarfing Airbus, which had sales last year of $8.8 billion, down from $9.6 billion in 1995.

The four-nation consortium is particularly angered by the exclusive supplier agreements signed by Boeing with U.S. airlines. Continental on Tuesday joined AMR Corp.'s American Airlines and Delta Air Lines Inc. in agreeing to buy all its planes from Boeing.
Airbus fears it is systematically being locked out of the vast U.S. airline market by these sole-supplier deals.
The commission has until July 31 to make a ruling on the $14 billion merger plan.

Boeing has historically held around 60 percent of the world civilian aircraft market and Airbus around 30 percent, with McDonnell Douglas accounting for the rest. McDonnell Douglas has a strong defence operation.
European aerospace executives say the significant government funding for defence research that McDonnell Dougals receives will support the merged company's civilian unit.
